summary: A chart legend for a float array: one row per entry with a swatch in the series tone (the same colour sequence as DonutChart's slices, by index), the label in onSurface and its share of the sum as a percent (or the value) in muted at the end of the row; one or two columns, filling the width.

values.doc: A float array, "@name" of resources.floatArrays (export it to let the host replace the data): the series the legend describes, in the order of `labels`; an entry's percent is its value over the array's sum

labels.doc: One label per entry, in the order of the array, e.g. ["Stocks", "Bonds", "Cash"]; fixed when the document is built. An entry may be "@name" of a root-level string variable the host sets

format.doc: What follows the label, at the end of the row in muted: percent (the entry's share of the sum, a whole number with %), value (the number itself, no decimals) or none

columns.doc: 1 or 2: two weighted columns, the entries alternating (0 2 4 on the left, 1 3 5 on the right)

color.doc: Series colour: the first swatch solid and each later one lighter (alpha 1 down to 0.3), the tones DonutChart gives its slices, so pass the donut's colour. In mono the swatches alternate filled and outlined

size.doc: Swatch side in dp (a rounded square); a row is size + 10 tall

maxEntries.doc: Rows from this index on are hidden, as are rows past the array's length

label.doc: Accessibility description of the whole legend; omitted, it is "Legend: N entries" from the labels

pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@shares" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list; labels is a JSON list written into the document ($each): a host can change the numbers but not the labels, so give one label per value the host may send. Rows past the array's length, or past maxEntries, collapse to 0 dp: each row's height is rowH * min(1, max(0, m - i)) over the local m = min(arrayLength(values), maxEntries), a tree variable at the head of the body. A visibility modifier cannot do this: it is an integer expression, which has no arrayLength and never sees a tree variable (U57), and the expander keeps a local that reads a float array out of resources.variables; a height expression is read at measure, in Java too (java-layout.sh: the collapsed row is 0 dp and the next content moves up). Each row clips to its bounds, so a collapsed swatch draws nothing

The swatches are the tones DonutChart gives its slices: paint alpha 1 - 0.7 * i / n over the same colour, so a Legend next to a DonutChart on the same array and `color` matches it by index. Pass the donut's `color` (secondary, success) when it is not primary. In mono the swatches alternate filled and outlined, as the donut's slices alternate thick and thin

The percent is round(100 * arrayGet(values, i) / sum) through textFromFloat (whole 3, decimal 0, flags 5) merged with "%"; rounded shares can add up to 99 or 101. format value prints the number with no decimals

columns 2 puts every entry in both columns and collapses the other column's half (an $if cannot test an index's parity), so a two-column legend costs twice the rows of a one-column one; use it for four to six short entries

Each row fills the width (the label sits in a weighted box, one line with an ellipsis, so a long label shortens instead of pushing the number out): in a row put the legend in a weighted box, or it has no width
